data.long_meaning: In Old English, Maddison is derived from the name Madyson, which is a compound of two Old English words: maeth meaning 'power' and duns meaning 'son'. The name Maddison is thought to have originated as a nickname for a powerful son, or as a variant of the Old English name Madoc, which means 'mighty one'. In English folklore, the name Madyson was also used as a name for a water spirit or mermaid. Therefore, Maddison can be interpreted as a 'gift of the sea' or a 'maiden of the sea'.
